question.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=-3x+3$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ The Fourier series of the $4$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and $f(x)=-3x+3$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(-3x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+3x]}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((-\frac{3}{2}\cdot {2}^{2}+3\cdot 2)-(-\frac{3}{2}\cdot (-2)^{2}+3\cdot (-2))) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0-(-12)) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
